title: Testing CIRCUS Circuit-Stability Ensembles on a Known GPT-2 Circuit

original_idea.body:
# Testing CIRCUS Circuit-Stability Ensembles on a Known GPT-2 Circuit

**Problem:** CIRCUS: Circuit Consensus under Uncertainty via Stability Ensembles (arXiv:2603.00523, March 2026) addresses the unreliability of discovered circuits by ensembling, but circuit-discovery instability is rarely quantified against a ground-truth circuit on a fixed model.

**Direction:** On GPT-2 small with TransformerLens, run a circuit-discovery method (e.g. attribution patching) multiple times with different seeds/data subsets on the indirect-object-identification task, measure variance in the recovered circuit, and test whether a simple stability-ensemble (intersection/consensus across runs) recovers the known IOI circuit more reliably than single runs.

**Why it matters:** Reproducibility of circuit discovery is foundational for trusting any interpretability claim; a small, honest stability study on a canonical circuit is broadly useful and needs only tiny models.

**Relevant context:** CIRCUS: Circuit Consensus under Uncertainty via Stability Ensembles (arXiv:2603.00523, March 2026); IOI circuit and TransformerLens are standard open tooling per subfield context.
